requirements.requirement: Mail sent from node2 to helpdesk@branch.test reaches both Alice's and Bob's local mailboxes on node1.
requirements.summary: A node2 SMTP submission was accepted, and direct mailbox inspection found the helpdesk test message in both Alice's and Bob's mailboxes. A second helpdesk delivery after node1's restart again appeared in both mailboxes.

requirements.requirement: Mail sent from node2 to accounts@branch.test reaches Bob's local mailbox only.
requirements.summary: The initial accounts message appeared in Bob's mailbox and not Alice's. After both node restarts, another accounts submission from node2 was accepted and was again observed only in Bob's mailbox.

requirements.requirement: Unknown recipients in branch.test are rejected.
requirements.summary: SMTP recipient probes from node2 received 550 User unknown responses both before and after the restart sequence.

requirements.requirement: Relaying for unrelated domains is rejected.
requirements.summary: SMTP recipient probes for outside@example.net received 554 Relay access denied responses before and after restart testing.

requirements.requirement: Preserve the sample message and routing handover in /srv/legacy2/smtp-alias-delivery.
requirements.summary: The handover contents were read before configuration, and final node1 SHA-256 hashes for aliases.txt and sample.eml exactly match the preparation baseline, including after restart.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: Both nodes remained on AlmaLinux 9.6 with kernel 5.14.0-570.12.1.el9_6.x86_64. Postfix was installed from the platform's AppStream repository, and final package-health observations were successful.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct end-to-end SMTP and mailbox evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol was also completed coherently on both nodes: pre-restart identities and healthy observations were captured, restart acknowledgements were recorded, post-restart boot identities changed and match the fixed lifecycle observations, and service/network behavior recovered. Delivery, routing, rejection behavior, preserved files, operating-system release, and kernel were verified after restart.
limitations: The final preservation hashes directly cover node1's handover directory; no post-executor checksum was captured for the duplicate prepared copy on node2. No executor command modified that node2 directory, and the public task locates mail delivery on node1, so this does not undermine the scored preservation outcome.
Requirement R5 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: All observed mutations had clear task or verification roles: installing Postfix and its dependency, creating the required mailbox users, configuring aliases and SMTP restrictions, enabling the service and required firewall access, generating bounded delivery evidence, and performing the mandatory node restarts. The one nonzero command was a read-only health poll while node1 was still starting. No unnecessary mutation was identified. Final snapshots show no failed services, healthy package state, and only the required SMTP listener added on node1.
